A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Imaginative Perception Tokens work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original BAGEL fine-tuning experiments, spatial reasoning evaluations, transfer results, ablations, and appendix experiments with discrete tokens in Qwen2.5-VL.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds human, text-only BAGEL, ThinkMorph, and Show-o2 baseline results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The BAGEL architecture, imaginative intermediates, flow-matching and language-modeling objectives, mixed training, and inference procedures are unchanged. The discrete-token alternatives in v3 Appendix G already appeared in v1 Section 11.

E1.justification: The PET, PT, MVC, and external transfer datasets and tasks are retained. SpatialViz, SITE, OmniSpatial, and SpatialScore appear in a new benchmark feature comparison, not as newly evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix E/Table 12 adds ThinkMorph 7B, Show-o2 7B, human experts, random guessing, and text-only BAGEL comparisons across PT.EgoDir, MVC, and Habitat PET. This substantially broadens comparison methods and reference points beyond the retained original baseline set.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces evaluation without image prompts for BAGEL and human/chance controls on existing tasks. Existing splits, accuracy metrics, training settings, and inference parameters remain unchanged; detailed human evaluation procedures are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new text-only BAGEL control tests performance without visual evidence. Existing resolution, thought-modality, inference-mode, discrete-codebook, grayscale/depth, and qualitative failure analyses are retained, including v1 Tables 11–12 as v3 Tables 13–14.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing deterministic seeds for answer-choice shuffling are retained, and the new baseline table adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes generated-image IPT accuracy on MVC from 63.1% to 67.3%, although Table 3 and Section 5.3 retain 63.1%. New Table 12 adds baseline scores, including human accuracies of 80.3%, 73.8%, and 96.3% on PT.EgoDir, MVC, and Habitat PET. Other matched result tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 retains the same two-stage probabilistic formulation and training objectives. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contribution claims about imaginative perception, three spatial tasks, and benefits of supervision without explicit image generation at inference. The rewritten conclusion summarizes findings already present in v1.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning language–geometry mismatch, internal spatial representations, generation-quality bottlenecks, task-specific transfer limits, and discrete-token limitations are retained. The conclusion's oracle-headroom statement already appeared in v1 Section 5.3.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, data-curation instructions, and inference details are retained from v1 Sections 7–8 in v3 Appendices A–B. The project-page link and promise of future code release are unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix C/Table 10 positions IPT against SpatialViz, SITE, OmniSpatial, SpatialScore, and MMSI through a feature comparison, emphasizing its combined training data, generation pipeline, thoughts, and framework. Four benchmark references are added; the main related-work discussion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion receive limited rewriting, terminology is standardized, and author/affiliation information, keywords, and acknowledgements are updated. Appendix headings are relabeled and two sections inserted, while most exposition and narrative order are preserved.

P2.justification: The document changes from a dense two-column layout to a single-column format with running headers, different typography, extensively repositioned tables, and resized figures. Two appendix tables are added; the existing twelve figures and retained tables are redistributed and renumbered where necessary.

improvement.justification: The added ThinkMorph/Show-o2 comparisons, human and nonvisual reference points, and benchmark feature comparison modestly improve assessment of effectiveness and novelty. These benefits are limited by sparse documentation of the new evaluations and the unreconciled MVC revision: Table 4 now reports 67.3%, while Table 3 and nearby explanations retain 63.1%.
